React names DOM attributes in its own way: `className` and not `class`, `htmlFor` and not `for`, `tabIndex` and not `tabindex`, `strokeWidth` and not `stroke-width`. Markup pasted from an HTML or SVG file has the other spelling, and React warns about it in the console when the page runs.

The rule checks elements with a lowercase name and reports three things:

- A name that React spells differently.
- A name that is not a DOM attribute at all.
- An attribute on an element it does not belong to, such as `checked` on a `<div>`.

Your own components, custom elements (a hyphen in the name, or an `is` attribute), and `data-*` attributes are not checked.

`--fix` renames an attribute when React has another spelling for it.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```jsx
const field = (
  <label class="field" for="email">
    Email <input id="email" tabindex="1" />
  </label>
);
```

{/* bad {"count": 2} */}
```jsx
const box = <div checked tooltip="Saved" />;
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
const field = (
  <label className="field" htmlFor="email">
    Email <input id="email" tabIndex="1" data-testid="email" />
  </label>
);

const card = <Card class="wide" tooltip="Saved" />;
const player = <video-player autostart="yes" />;
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ignore` | `[]` | Names of attributes to accept as they are. |
| `requireDataLowercase` | `false` | Report a `data-*` attribute with an uppercase letter in its name, on any element. |

Use `ignore` for attributes that a library adds, such as the `css` prop of Emotion:

{/* good {"options": [{"ignore": ["css"]}]} */}
```jsx
const box = <div css={{ display: "flex" }} />;
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"requireDataLowercase": true}]} */}
```jsx
const button = <button data-testID="save">Save</button>;
```
